context: batch s150c, independent S8 audit: three new psychiatry briefs built on decision spine v2 from the 2026-10-23b board intake: dementia (a presentation hub), eating-disorders (a disease brief) and defense-mechanisms (the page's first lookup brief), each audited whole

types.dementia: presentation hub (data-entry hub; cognitive decline in an adult: DLB, Alzheimer, vascular, frontotemporal, CJD, Korsakoff and reversible causes), psychiatry; steps 5 to 8 greyed; treatment by cause inside step 4; review in full
types.eating-disorders: disease brief (anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder, ARFID; diabetic gastroparesis as the medical mimic), psychiatry; review in full
types.defense-mechanisms: lookup brief (SPINE_SPEC entry type: tables plus one commitment rule, no spine): bottom line, intro line, immature and mature tables (names masked in study mode), a commonly-confused-pairs table and one commitment rule as the pause point; no stepper or numbered steps by design; review in full

acc: A hub may carry treatment no other live brief owns inside step 4 Workup, after the workup tree; steps 5 to 8 stay greyed (Jonathan 2026-10-18).

Where a board source (AnKing card, UWorld, NBME) and a guideline differ, the brief teaches the board answer and puts the guideline in an "In practice:" hover (runbook section 3): the hover is intended, not a finding.
Word counts are not judged (2026-10-19 layers rule: nothing is cut for length).

dementia, frontotemporal dementia: one UWorld explanation mentions impaired memory, the UWorld DLB library page says memory and visuospatial function are spared early; the brief teaches early sparing (lead call 3). Judge whether the line as written is accurate for Step 2.

eating-disorders: only the adult BMI cutoff (under 18.5) is taught because the cards disagree on the percentile for patients 20 or younger (5th versus 10th); the omission is a recorded scope call (lead call 4), not a finding.
dementia, CJD: 14-3-3 is taught as supportive and nonspecific, RT-QuIC as the confirmatory test (lead call 5).
eating-disorders: gastroparesis treatment is the last rung of the treatment ladder because the mimic has no owner brief (lead call 8).
defense-mechanisms: having no steps, workup or treatment is the lookup entry type, not a finding.
This is the independent S8 audit (the launch budget names it). You have not seen any earlier receipt or the lead's adjudication: judge the brief cold, as a fresh accuracy reviewer would.

Claim-level entailment (the s150b audit's MED C class): for every claim, each action, test, drug, threshold or recommendation the line states must be stated by one of its cited facts (claim_map.json ids, quotes in facts.json); a fact about the same topic is not enough. Report a stated action no cited quote states.

Card child coverage (the s150b audit's MED D class): for each card marked covered:S### in cards_disposition.json, read the card's high-yield lines in cards.md and check that the named claims teach each high-yield statement, including a child statement inherited from its parent card; report a covered card whose named claims teach a different part of the card.
Layers rule (Jonathan 2026-10-19): a fact a board item keys (the answer, or the clue that rules out a distractor) must stay visible, not only in a hover. Report a keyed fact found only in a hover.

Brief set rules (Jonathan 2026-10-20): every practice item carries three reasons ("reasons: key | d1 | d2" on its item line), each the choice's defining feature or the fact in the stem that rules it out; a distractor that is a differential row reuses that row's wording. Judge each reason for Step 2 truth on that stem and agreement with the body and the item's explanation.
Every age, cutoff, duration and interval against the cited quote and the board sources in facts.json (kind board first).
Card dispositions: spot-check that each "covered" card's fact is taught by the claims it names, and that no carded fact the bank tests is marked scope or not-topic.
